transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you saw a problem that wasn't yours to fix, and you fixed it anyway.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Our checkout service was timing out for mobile users. It was the platform team's service. I traced the latency spike using Jaeger, found an N+1 query, wrote a PR with the fix and a benchmark showing 60% latency reduction, and got it merged.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What did you do after the fix was merged?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I added a Datadog monitor for that query pattern so if cardinality grew again we'd catch it in staging. The platform lead was grateful.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: The backend lead and I disagreed about whether the API should be versioned from day one. I proposed we look at three similar systems and measure the cost. The data showed two of three had significant rework. We designed a lightweight versioning scheme.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I was an enthusiastic advocate for event-driven architecture before we had enough domain complexity. My team spent a sprint building a Kafka pipeline that a polling job would have solved in two days. I wrote it up as a learning doc and added a decision checklist.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What's a weakness you've had to actively work on?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I have a pattern of under-communicating when I'm uncertain. I go quiet in planning meetings. My manager flagged this. I started being explicit about confidence levels and it became natural.
